title: Agricultural monitoring with Machine Learning
description: Web application for crop monitoring that integrates IoT sensor data analysis with Python and ML, immutable traceability on AWS QLDB and real-time visualizations for crop alerts.

problem.title: The Problem
problem.intro: A client in Spain needs to monitor crops in real time from IoT sensor data spread across the field. The data arrives scattered, the history is not auditable and alerts arrive too late.
items: Scattered IoT sensor data with no reliable history
No auditable traceability of the data feeding decisions
Late crop alerts due to a lack of automated analysis
A team without a unified view of crop status

phases.title: 1. Data analysis with Python + Colab
phases.description: Modeled the sensor data analysis with Python in Google Colab, understanding moisture, temperature and irrigation patterns.
items: EDA of IoT sensor data to detect crop patterns
Data pipeline preparation with Scikit-learn for early signals
Fast prototyping in Colab before productizing

phases.title: 2. Nightly sync to AWS QLDB
phases.description: Architected a nightly synchronization of sensor data into AWS QLDB, guaranteeing immutable traceability.
items: QLDB ledger as the single source of truth for sensor history
Automated nightly sync with AWS Lambda and EventBridge
Every piece of history stays immutable and auditable

phases.title: 3. Real-time visualizations and alerts
phases.description: Built the web UI with real-time visualizations for crop insights and automated alerts.
items: Real-time visualizations with Matplotlib and Seaborn
Automated alerts by crop thresholds agreed with the client
Angular frontend consuming the Node.js API

phases.title: 4. R&D audit
phases.description: The project went through an R&D audit, validating the data design and the methodology used.
items: Data pipeline documentation for the audit
QLDB traceability validated as a quality guarantee
Closed with the R&D team's findings

subsections.title: Data with auditable backing
subsections.description: The sensor history stops being a lost file: every reading lands in an immutable ledger.
items: AWS QLDB as an immutable record of sensor history
Full traceability: what data, from which sensor, at what time
Foundation for data audits and informed decisions

subsections.title: Productized ML analysis
subsections.description: What started as a Colab prototype ended as a production pipeline.
items: Data pipeline with Python + Scikit-learn
Moisture, temperature and irrigation signal analysis
Automated nightly sync with no manual intervention

subsections.title: Real-time visibility
subsections.description: The team sees crop status up to date and receives automatic alerts.
items: Real-time visualizations with Matplotlib/Seaborn
Automated crop alerts by thresholds
A single unified view of the field for the team

items.label: Prototype to production:
items.text: starting in Colab accelerated hypothesis validation before investing in infrastructure.

items.label: Ledger as an asset:
items.text: QLDB turned the history into an auditable asset instead of a loose data repository.

items.label: Alerts that arrive on their own:
items.text: automating the sync is what made the operational difference: without a pipeline, there are no alerts.
